newsitem.title: SPAIN: Air Europa plans twice-weekly Madrid-Miami link.
newsitem.headline: Air Europa plans twice-weekly Madrid-Miami link.

text.p: Spanish carrier Air Europa plans to start twice-weekly flights from Madrid to Miami and on to Cancun in Mexico, using a Boeing 767-200 aircraft, a cargo official at the airline said.
The charter passenger flights are scheduled to start on November 7 and will give Air Europa considerable cargo capacity on the route.
"We're now engaged in acquiring pallets and are looking at tariffs," the official told Reuters.
Current market rates ex-Madrid to Miami are between 150 and 200 pesetas per kg for a 100 kg shipment, while Mexico is in the 250 to 300 peseta range, market sources said.

Air Europa now has only one Boeing 767 but it plans to take delivery of one or two more next Spring to use regularly on its existing Madrid-New York service, instead of the current Boeing 757, the official said.

Air Europa's cargo traffic from Madrid to New York is relatively modest at present, not least because the Boeing 757 with the wind against it at take-off, as is usually the case in Madrid, can carry no more than 1,000 kg of cargo, he added.
But the airline makes better use of the return flight, bringing goods bound for many destinations in Spain including the Canary Islands, the official said.

Air Europa, majority-owned by chairman Juan Jose Hidalgo, has been steadily expanding its scheduled flight business since 1994. It forecasts revenues of around 60 billion pesetas this year, up from 48 billion in 1995.
